note: Real run 2026-11-20: FANUC CRX-5iA product page (fanucamerica.com) read by real Claude Sonnet extract; manufacturer values as extracted and verified by code. Frames and parsed URDF removed.

manufacturer_spec.kinematics_note: 6-axis collaborative robot arm (J1 to J6). The page gives total motion range per joint (J1 380°, J2 360°, J3 380°, J4 380°, J5 360°, J6 450°), not min/max limits. Mounting is floor, angle or inverted. Controller is R-30iB Plus.

robot.name: FANUC CRX-5iA
robot.rationale: Built from verified datasheet values. dof=6 from the datasheet; per-joint lists reset to family defaults Link lengths (upper_arm_m, forearm_m, wrist_m) are not published: the generated arm's segments were scaled so the reach equals the verified 0.994 m (shoulder to wrist-flange, stretched out) Link masses are the generated ones scaled to the verified total mass (distribution assumed)

differences.impact: Both arms reach well beyond the farthest point the task needs, so A and B are reachable with either one.
This minimum distance was not checked for either arm, so we can't say from the simulation whether the near points are a problem.
Both arms have more than enough height on paper, but this was not formally checked. The difference between them does not matter for this task.
Whether either arm can reach down to table height was not checked, so it remains unconfirmed. Both are listed the same.
The generated arm is sized exactly to the load, so it has no spare margin. The product carries about five times what is needed.
Both arms move the tool comfortably faster than the task requires.
Both arms can speed up and slow down far faster than needed, so there is plenty of margin.
The grip is only just above what is needed to hold the bottle, so there is very little margin for both. The result is the same for each.
Both just meet the 6 s cycle with no spare time, so any delay would drop below 10 bottles per minute. The result is the same for each.
Both repeat positions far more tightly than the ±5 mm placement needs. The product is even tighter, which the task does not require.
No joint-limit result is available for either arm, so nothing can be said here.
The base joint carries essentially no holding load in this task, so both are fine.
Both shoulder joints can hold the load with a wide margin. The product's own requirement is higher because the arm itself is heavier.
Both elbow joints hold the load with margin. The generated arm has the tighter margin of the two.
The wrist joint sees almost no load, so both pass easily.
There is no result for the generated arm's joint 5. The product's joint 5 sees no load and passes.
There is no result for the generated arm's joint 6. The product's joint 6 sees no load and passes.
The base joint can turn faster than the move needs on both arms, so speed is not a concern.
No collision check was available for either arm, so clearance around the table is not confirmed.
The product is rated for much more than the bottle and gripper weigh, while the generated arm is sized just to the load. Both cover the task.
Both are well inside the ±5 mm placement tolerance. The product's finer precision goes beyond what the task needs.
